scientific_interpretation: The amended sort changes retrieval order, not the registered literal queries, date window, or eligibility population definition. Its operational effect does not guarantee an immutable database snapshot: citation counts and records can change during collection, and ties remain possible.

The final reports support observed consistency across the exact 64 complete calendar-year partitions, with 414 pages and 38,137 new occurrences. The root's independent raw-page revalidation remains the separate evidence for the underlying response chains.

Every one of the 31,429 old provider IDs remains in the new 31,471-ID union, and all 38,127 old occurrence objects are preserved. The 42 new-only IDs are candidate additions requiring ordinary identity/date and eligibility review, not automatic inclusions.

The old inventory has 38,083 unique query-ID pairs plus 44 repeated same-query occurrences. New-only IDs contribute 44 query memberships, and nine shared IDs gain ten more. Thus 38,127 - 44 + 44 + 10 = 38,137 new occurrences without any identity or query-membership loss.

The strongest supported claim is OBSERVED_PARTITION_ENUMERATION_CONSISTENT. This is neither an inclusion freeze nor a scientific proportion estimate. Known-source candidates, backward references, source-version/date reconciliation, primary-source eligibility, unresolved access, and independent coding remain separate coverage work.
The reviewed final summary correctly leaves global_p_lit_complete, database_search_complete, and inclusion_list_frozen false.
